title: Notion Worker Exploration
html:
Notion workers allow you a simple way to let you extend Notion with custom backend logic without managing servers for three main use cases that I can tell.

You can sync external data into Notion, maybe pull data from Salesforce, Stripe, GitHub, SoundCloud, etc. into Notion databases on a recurring schedule, so Notion becomes a live mirror of external systems.

You can give Notion AI agents new abilities register “tools” that your Custom Agents can call, like “create a Jira ticket” or “look up a customer record,” turning Notion AI into something that can act on external systems, not just read/write Notion content.

You could receive web hooks and let external services (GitHub pushes, Stripe payments, etc.) trigger code that runs inside Notion’s infrastructure.

Basically it seems like the point is to turn Notion from a passive workspace into a hub that connects to and automates with the rest of your stack without you needing to spin up your own server or stitch together Zapier type automations. Notion hosts and runs the code; you just write and deploy it via their CLI.

This could be relevant for things like syncing CRM/account data into Notion dashboards, or building internal tools a team uses inside Notion.
